sourceHtml:
Google is centering its development environment around AI agents at the Android Dev Summit. The updates include integrations for Anthropic and OpenAI models, new APIs for local smartphone agents, and a pair of smart glasses.

Google introduced updates for its developer tools and system APIs at this year's Android Dev Summit. Opening up the Android Studio development environment was the main focus.

With Android Studio Rabbit 2, Google is launching a "Bring Your Own Agent" (BYOA) feature. Developers are no longer limited to Google's own AI tools. Instead, they can use the open Agent Client Protocol (ACP) to run more than 40 different coding agents directly in the IDE.

Developers can install and simultaneously run Anthropic's Claude Agent, OpenAI's Codex, and Google Antigravity through the built-in marketplace. These agents get direct access to IDE tools like project structure, symbol resolution, the emulator, and the Logcat system.

Google also released version 2.0 of the Android Bench leaderboard to measure AI model performance on complex tasks. It evaluates language models on multi-day development projects based on functionality, time spent, and cost.

AI-generated code changes often get messy, so Google is adding a code verification tool called Change Review. It analyzes pending changes, generates bug reports, and explains modifications step by step. The Android Studio Canary preview also adds a migration assistant that automatically translates older XML layouts into Jetpack Compose. Meanwhile, Google is testing Lightbuild, a declarative build system based on a YAML schema that both humans and AI agents can read and edit.

New terminal tools and specialized skills cut token usage for coding agents

Google expanded the Android CLI command-line tool for developers who run their agents in the terminal or in CI pipelines. It is now available as an official agent plugin for Claude Code, OpenAI's Codex, and Google Antigravity.

New commands let AI agents render Compose previews in the terminal to visually check UI changes without booting up an emulator. Internal Google tests show agents finished UI tasks 77 percent faster and used up to three times fewer tokens with this feature. The CLI also supports streaming physical test devices from Google labs so agents can investigate device-specific bugs.

Debugging and performance analysis got new features too. Google built the open-source LeakCanary memory leak detection library into both the CLI and the Android Studio Profiler. The system evaluates heap dumps on the computer instead of the mobile device, which keeps the app from slowing down during testing. In a Google A/B test using Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 model, the CLI tool helped find and fix memory leaks nearly twice as fast while cutting token usage by about 25 percent.

Other command-line tools let agents capture system traces via the Android Performance Analyzer, pull crash reports from Firebase Crashlytics, or check code optimization through the R8 compiler. Language models often lack training on the newest APIs, so Google now provides over 30 Android Skills. These feed documentation to agents for tasks like checking Google Play policies before app submission, handling permission security issues, or adapting layouts for foldables and laptops branded as Googlebooks.

Gemini Nano 4 and MCP turn Android apps into interactive agent tools

Beyond developer tools, Google is shipping new APIs to build agent features into apps or connect apps to system agents. For local on-device processing, Google is adding an alpha Agentic API powered by Gemini Nano 4 to its ML Kit. This interface automatically executes functions, saves chat history, manages the orchestration loop, and provides safety filters.

Google is using the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and launching the AppFunctions API in beta as a unified tool-calling layer so apps can share functions with local or system-wide agents. The new alpha Agent-to-UI (A2UI) interface for Jetpack Compose builds on this. Instead of replying with plain text blocks, agents can display interactive user interfaces built from the specific app's components.

To bring these app services into Google Search and the Gemini app, the company is launching a preview of the Connected Apps Platform. Developers can link their apps via Android MCP or cloud-hosted MCP servers and manage them through a single console. Google says over 50 partner integrations from companies like Adobe, Peloton, and Experian are already live in the Gemini app, and they will roll out to web search in the coming weeks.

XREAL AURA smart glasses bring Android XR and Gemini into the real world

Google also announced updates for several hardware form factors. Updates to Jetpack Compose 1.13 and the AppState model make it easier to adapt apps for large screens, and the Extended Reality (XR) development environment is leaving the testing phase. The Jetpack XR SDK, the XR emulators in Android Studio, and the Engine Hub for Unity, Godot, and Unreal are now available as stable releases.

Alongside the software updates, Google partnered with hardware maker XREAL to unveil the XREAL AURA. XR chief Shahram Izadi says they are the first wired smart glasses running Android XR. The glasses weigh under 95 grams and feature transparent, dimmable lenses with a 70-degree field of view. The computing unit and battery sit in an external puck that doubles as a trackpad and runs on Qualcomm's new Snapdragon Reality Elite chip.

Users can place up to five Android apps in their field of view at once or plug in a USB-C cable to mirror their laptop screen. Gemini is built in here too. The AI can see both the real-world environment through the glasses and the virtual screens, allowing it to organize windows, offer video game tips, or visually highlight physical objects in the room. The XREAL AURA is available to order now in the US, Canada, and South Korea for $1,099, with shipping set to begin in mid-November.

translation.html:
Google 在 Android Dev Summit 上将 AI 智能体置于开发环境的核心。此次更新包括对 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 模型的集成、面向手机端本地智能体的新 API，以及一款智能眼镜。

Google 在今年的 Android Dev Summit 上介绍了开发工具和系统 API 的更新，重点是开放 Android Studio 开发环境。

随着 Android Studio Rabbit 2 的推出，Google 正在上线“自带智能体”（Bring Your Own Agent，BYOA）功能。开发者不再局限于 Google 自家的 AI 工具，而是可以通过开放的 Agent Client Protocol（ACP），直接在 IDE 中运行 40 多种不同的编程智能体。

开发者可以通过内置市场安装并同时运行 Anthropic 的 Claude Agent、OpenAI 的 Codex 和 Google Antigravity。这些智能体可以直接访问 IDE 工具，包括项目结构、符号解析、模拟器和 Logcat 系统。

Google 还发布了 Android Bench 排行榜的 2.0 版本，用于衡量 AI 模型处理复杂任务的表现。它以需要数天完成的开发项目为基础，从功能实现、耗时和成本三个方面评估语言模型。

AI 生成的代码改动往往容易变得混乱，因此 Google 正在加入一款名为 Change Review 的代码验证工具。它会分析待处理的改动、生成缺陷报告，并逐步解释修改内容。Android Studio Canary 预览版还新增了迁移助手，可自动将旧版 XML 布局转换为 Jetpack Compose。与此同时，Google 正在测试 Lightbuild，这是一套基于 YAML 模式的声明式构建系统，人类和 AI 智能体都可以阅读和编辑。

新的终端工具和专项技能降低编程智能体的 token 用量

Google 扩展了 Android CLI 命令行工具，面向在终端或 CI 流水线中运行智能体的开发者。它现已作为官方智能体插件提供，支持 Claude Code、OpenAI 的 Codex 和 Google Antigravity。

新命令允许 AI 智能体在终端中渲染 Compose 预览，无需启动模拟器就能以可视方式检查 UI 改动。Google 内部测试显示，使用该功能后，智能体完成 UI 任务的速度提高了 77%，token 用量最低降至原来的三分之一。CLI 还支持以流式连接方式使用实体测试设备，这些设备来自 Google 实验室，可供智能体排查特定设备上的缺陷。

调试和性能分析也获得了新功能。Google 将开源内存泄漏检测库 LeakCanary 集成到了 CLI 和 Android Studio Profiler 中。系统在电脑上而非移动设备上分析堆转储，避免应用在测试过程中变慢。在 Google 使用 Anthropic 的 Claude Opus 5.5 模型开展的一项 A/B 测试中，CLI 工具帮助查找和修复内存泄漏的速度接近原来的两倍，同时将 token 用量减少了约 25%。

其他命令行工具允许智能体通过 Android Performance Analyzer 采集系统跟踪记录，从 Firebase Crashlytics 拉取崩溃报告，或通过 R8 编译器检查代码优化情况。语言模型往往缺乏针对最新 API 的训练，因此 Google 现在提供了 30 多项 Android Skills。这些技能会为智能体提供文档，帮助其完成应用提交前检查 Google Play 政策、处理权限安全问题，或为折叠屏设备和以 Googlebooks 为品牌的笔记本电脑适配布局等任务。

Gemini Nano 4 和 MCP 将 Android 应用变成可交互的智能体工具

除了开发工具，Google 还在推出新的 API，用于在应用中构建智能体功能，或将应用连接到系统智能体。针对设备端本地处理，Google 正在其 ML Kit 中加入由 Gemini Nano 4 驱动的 Alpha 版 Agentic API。该接口会自动执行函数、保存聊天记录、管理编排循环，并提供安全过滤器。

Google 正在采用 Model Context Protocol（MCP），并推出 Beta 版 AppFunctions API，将其作为统一的工具调用层，让应用能够与本地智能体或系统级智能体共享函数。面向 Jetpack Compose 的全新 Alpha 版 Agent-to-UI（A2UI）接口以此为基础。智能体可以使用特定应用的组件构建并展示交互式用户界面，而不再仅以纯文本块回复。

为了将这些应用服务引入 Google 搜索和 Gemini 应用，Google 正在推出 Connected Apps Platform 预览版。开发者可以通过 Android MCP 或云端托管的 MCP 服务器连接应用，并通过一个控制台统一管理。Google 表示，来自 Adobe、Peloton 和 Experian 等公司的 50 多项合作伙伴集成已在 Gemini 应用中上线，并将在未来几周内逐步推广至网页搜索。

XREAL AURA 智能眼镜将 Android XR 和 Gemini 带入现实世界

Google 还宣布了面向多种硬件形态的更新。Jetpack Compose 1.13 和 AppState 模型的更新让应用更容易适配大屏幕，扩展现实（XR）开发环境也将结束测试阶段。Jetpack XR SDK、Android Studio 中的 XR 模拟器，以及面向 Unity、Godot 和 Unreal 的 Engine Hub 现均已提供稳定版。

在发布软件更新的同时，Google 与硬件制造商 XREAL 合作推出了 XREAL AURA。XR 负责人 Shahram Izadi 表示，这是首款运行 Android XR 的有线智能眼镜。眼镜重量不到 95 克，配备透明且可调光的镜片，视场角为 70 度。计算单元和电池位于一个外置圆盘形设备中，该设备也可兼作触控板，并搭载高通全新的 Snapdragon Reality Elite 芯片。

用户可以在视野中同时放置最多五个 Android 应用，也可以插入 USB-C 线缆，镜像显示笔记本电脑屏幕。眼镜还内置了 Gemini。AI 既能通过眼镜看到现实环境，也能看到虚拟屏幕，因此可以整理窗口、提供电子游戏提示，或以可视方式突出显示房间中的实物。XREAL AURA 现已在美国、加拿大和韩国开放订购，售价为 1,099 美元，计划于 11 月中旬开始发货。
